title: Many mansions (John 14:1–6)
hook: let not your heart be troubled; I am the way, the truth and the life

segments.voice: Yesterday, mandatum, love as I have loved you. Your line was by this they will know. What did you do that someone could see? Day five hundred eighteen.

Arriving somewhere strange is easier when someone says, we've set up the spare room for you. Clean sheets, a towel folded on the bed, maybe a glass of water on the nightstand. The bag isn't even unpacked, and already there's a place for you. At the supper, Jesus has just told Peter that he'll deny him three times before the rooster crows. It's a hard thing to hear. And the very next thing Jesus says is about rooms.
screen: `THE SPARE ROOM, READY.` → `PETER WILL DENY HIM.` → `THEN, ROOMS.`

segments.voice: In the Douay-Rheims: "Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many mansions. If not, I would have told you: because I go to prepare a place for you." Mansions sounds like marble and gated driveways. In the Douay's older English, the word just meant a dwelling, a place to stay; the Latin behind it is mansiones, lodgings. So this isn't real estate. It's: there is room for you to stay, and I'm going ahead to get it ready. Then Thomas says out loud what he doesn't understand: Lord, we don't know where you're going, so how can we know the way? And Jesus answers: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No man cometh to the Father, but by me." Thomas asked for directions. He gets a person. And notice who Jesus said it to: frightened men, one of whom was about to deny him and all of whom, he will soon tell them, would be scattered. He doesn't wait for them to be brave first. He gives the promise while they are still afraid, and the room is ready before they are.
screen: `LET NOT YOUR HEART BE TROUBLED.` · `MANSIONS: PLACES TO STAY.` · `THOMAS ASKS THE WAY.` · `SAID TO FRIGHTENED MEN.` · then, large: `MANY MANSIONS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold someone who is afraid of dying. It might be someone sick right now, someone very old, someone grieving, or a fear you carry yourself. Sit, and let your breathing slow. Picture them in a quiet room, a light on, a chair ready. Don't try to argue the fear away. Just keep them company in your mind. If you pray, you can pray for them with Jesus's words, let not your heart be troubled. If you don't, simply hold them kindly. The bell holds the time.
Many mansions. In his Father's house there are many places to stay, and Jesus goes ahead to prepare one. Today's word.

Your line: a place for you. Today, make room for someone: a seat saved, a chair pulled out, a call returned. And that's week seventy-four, all from John: kalos, anastasis, the house filled with nard, the grain of wheat, the towel, mandatum, and many mansions. Day five hundred eighteen.

howItsDone: John 14:1–6 is one of the Gospel readings offered for Catholic funeral Masses, and the Church prays daily for the dying and the dead, especially in November.

fork.setup: you're Thomas. Jesus says you know the way to where he's going. you don't. what do you do?
options: say so: Lord, we don't know where you're going.
fork.reveal: Thomas admits it out loud, and gets the answer: I am the way, and the truth, and the life.

trapdoor: what you thought: big houses in heaven.
what it means: places to stay, prepared ahead, for frightened friends who haven't yet proved brave.
what a scholar hears: the Douay follows the Latin mansiones, lodgings; and the promise comes straight after Peter's denial is foretold (13:38).
recall: lit in the temple court at the feast
